Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-defined cavitary lesion in the right upper lung zone containing a rounded soft-tissue mass separated from the cavity wall by a radiolucent crescent of air (the air crescent sign), which is pathognomonic for an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is consistent with colonization of a pre-existing pulmonary cavity, a known complication in patients with underlying structural lung disease.
